2609.39958.title: Better Deck or Different Judge? Evaluating Agentic Harness Gains in Corporate and Investment Banking
2609.39958.paper_summary: Corporate and investment banking teams use presentations to support credit decisions and advise clients on financing and transactions. Producing these decks requires reconciling financial data, tracing sources and turning analysis into a recommendation. We retrospectively study the development of an agentic harness combining a 27B language model, financial calculations, narrative templates and validation checks. LLM judges guide engineering changes and assess the resulting decks, raising the question of whether higher scores reflect better documents or changes in grading. In shared-session text-only grading with template markers removed, five judges score the complete system 20.4 to 33.6 points out of 95 above the same model generating directly from a short prompt. Every judge scores the system higher on all seventeen development deliverables. Margins against direct Opus generation from a short prompt range from -4.7 to +0.8 points. Judges agree on broad progress across development rounds but agree less on final-deck rankings than on pooled scores. Repeated grading also shifts scores on unchanged decks, making small improvements difficult to distinguish from judge variability.
2609.39958.paper_summary_zh: 企業和投資銀行團隊使用簡報來支持信貸決策並為客戶提供融資和交易建議。製作這些簡報需要調和財務數據、追溯來源並將分析轉化為建議。我們回顧性地研究了一種結合27B語言模型、財務計算、敘事模板和驗證檢查的代理式工具的發展。LLM評審指導工程變更並評估所產生的簡報，提出了更高分數是否反映更好的文件或評分變化的問題。在去除模板標記的共享會議文本評分中，五位評審將完整系統的分數評為20.4到33.6分（滿分95分），高於直接從簡短提示生成的同一模型。每位評審在所有十七個開發交付物上均給予系統更高的分數。與直接從簡短提示生成的Opus相比，分數差距範圍從-4.7到+0.8分。評審們在開發回合的整體進展上達成一致，但對最終簡報的排名共識較少，與集中分數相比。重複評分也會改變未變更簡報的分數，使小幅改進難以與評審變異區分開來。
